title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Arteta targets the end of the Anfield curse
standfirst: Arsenal arrive at Anfield after a midweek cup exit at Fleetwood, while Liverpool are unbeaten in five.

title: Racing Santander v Real Madrid: Mbappé storm follows the leaders' run
standfirst: Real Madrid have won five in a row, but the build-up has been dominated by Kylian Mbappé's apology and a broadcasting row in China.

title: Juventus v Napoli: Spalletti under pressure after Genoa defeat
standfirst: Juventus have lost three of their nine Serie A games, and reports describe unrest in the dressing room before the visit of Napoli.

title: Athletic Club v Real Sociedad: the first Basque derby of the season
standfirst: Real Sociedad arrive at San Mamés with four straight league wins, and Athletic still remember last season's four derby defeats.

title: Marseille v Toulouse: OM look to steady after the Le Havre scare
standfirst: Marseille led Le Havre 4-0 and nearly lost it; Toulouse arrive unbeaten in five Ligue 1 games.

title: Lyon v Angers: Fonseca's future in question as injuries pile up
standfirst: Reports link Paulo Fonseca with Sporting CP, and Lyon go into the game with Ernest Nuamah expected to lead the attack.

title: Paris FC v Monaco: a double-header Sunday for the capital club
standfirst: Paris FC host Paris Saint-Germain's women and Monaco on the same afternoon, in Pierre Ferracci's last home games as president.

title: Eintracht Frankfurt v Hamburg: a rematch five days after the cup tie
standfirst: Frankfurt won 3-1 in Hamburg in the DFB-Pokal on Tuesday, and HSV's injury list has only grown since.

title: Lecce v Genoa: De Rossi's side ride the Juventus win
standfirst: Genoa beat Juventus 2-0 in midweek; Lecce have lost four of their last five.

title: Elche v Valencia: Aguirre still chasing a first win
standfirst: Valencia are winless in four, while Elche are unbeaten in five ahead of the derby at the Martínez Valero.

title: Union Berlin v Cologne: a second meeting in five days
standfirst: Cologne beat Union 5-0 in midweek; now the two sides meet again in the Bundesliga in Berlin.

title: Sassuolo v Fiorentina: two teams without a win in five
standfirst: Sassuolo conceded six to Lazio, while Fiorentina sit in the relegation zone and have lost Nikola Pongračić.

title: Lorient v Brest: the postponed Breton derby
standfirst: The derby moved because of last weekend's protests now goes ahead on Monday, with Lorient unbeaten in three.

title: Atalanta v Parma: Sarri under pressure amid an injury crisis
standfirst: Atalanta are without a win in four and have lost Gianluca Scamacca, while reports in Bergamo mention Igor Tudor.

title: Galatasaray v Stuttgart: in-form hosts meet the Leverkusen conquerors
standfirst: Galatasaray have won four in a row; Stuttgart arrive after a 4-2 win at Bayer Leverkusen.

title: Atlético Madrid v Bayern Munich: injury worries for the Bavarians
standfirst: Bayern drew with Dortmund and lost three players to injury, while Atlético arrive on seven straight league wins.

title: Barcelona v Aston Villa: Flick's side back on track
standfirst: Barcelona hit Alavés for six; Villa drew with Fulham after Zion Suzuki's own goal.

title: Bodø/Glimt v Lille: title race heat meets Giroud's late show
standfirst: Bodø/Glimt won a fiery top game against Viking; Lille beat Lens with an 86th-minute goal from Olivier Giroud.

title: Feyenoord v Inter: two sides looking to bounce back
standfirst: Feyenoord dropped points at home to Fortuna Sittard, while Inter lost the Milan derby.

title: Manchester United v Roma: Carrick's crisis meets Gasperini's unbeaten side
standfirst: United are winless in nine and have lost three in a row; Roma are unbeaten in Serie A.

title: Villarreal v Paris Saint-Germain: the champions on nine straight wins
standfirst: PSG arrive after a 5-1 win at Le Havre; Felix Zwayer will referee the game.

title: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United: Martinez sees red as Carrick's pain deepens
standfirst: Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer struck after the break as ten-man Manchester United fell apart at Stamford Bridge.

title: Manchester City 0-1 Brighton: Ayari strike sinks the leaders at the Etihad
standfirst: Yasin Ayari's early finish gave Brighton revenge for their midweek cup exit and handed Manchester City a second straight league defeat.

title: Bayer Leverkusen 2-4 VfB Stuttgart: Demirovic double stuns the BayArena
standfirst: Stuttgart soaked up pressure and struck four times on the break and from set pieces to win a six-goal contest in Leverkusen.

title: Coventry City 3-1 Sunderland: Sky Blues climb out of the drop zone
standfirst: Goals from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni lifted Coventry out of the bottom three and left ten-man Sunderland at the foot of the table.

title: Levante 0-2 Atlético Madrid: Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone seal it
standfirst: Atlético Madrid were clinical in Valencia, scoring either side of the break while Levante fired 20 shots for no reward.

title: Feyenoord 1-1 Fortuna Sittard: Late 't Zand leveller silences De Kuip
standfirst: Shiloh 't Zand struck four minutes from time to cancel out Luciano Valente's opener and deny Feyenoord victory.

title: Hull City 2-2 Ipswich Town: Enciso salvages a point at the MKM
standfirst: Hull fought back from a goal down to lead through Oliver McBurnie's free-kick, only for Julio Enciso to equalise six minutes later.

title: Bologna 2-1 Monza: Skorupski save settles a three-penalty contest
standfirst: Bologna came from behind through Tommaso Pobega and a Federico Bernardeschi penalty, then Lukasz Skorupski saved from the spot.

title: Schalke 04 0-2 RB Leipzig: Nusa leads the way at the Veltins Arena
standfirst: Antonio Nusa scored a penalty and set up Rômulo as RB Leipzig overpowered Schalke with ten shots on target.

title: Rayo Vallecano 3-0 Celta Vigo: De Frutos double powers Rayo
standfirst: Jorge de Frutos scored twice and Unai López added a third as Rayo cruised past a Celta side who failed to hit the target.

title: Brentford 2-0 Nottingham Forest: Milenkovic own goal sets up Bees win
standfirst: A freak own goal and a deflected Igor Thiago finish ended Brentford's winless run and left Forest in the bottom three.

title: FC Augsburg 1-2 SC Freiburg: Irié header completes Freiburg comeback
standfirst: Freiburg turned around a first-half deficit with two second-half goals from just two shots on target.

title: AFC Bournemouth 2-0 Leeds United: Trafford error gifts Cherries win
standfirst: Evanilson capitalised on a goalkeeping mistake and substitute Amine Adli sealed Bournemouth's third straight league win.

title: Werder Bremen 2-0 TSG Hoffenheim: Füllkrug and Dinkçi strike
standfirst: Niclas Füllkrug and Eren Dinkçi scored in the second half as Werder Bremen beat a Hoffenheim side who dominated the ball.

title: Borussia Mönchengladbach 0-0 SC Paderborn: Stalemate at Borussia-Park
standfirst: Neither side found a way through in an evenly matched goalless draw in Mönchengladbach.

title: Der Klassiker without Kompany: Danks takes Bayern's bench against Dortmund
standfirst: Vincent Kompany is recovering at home after collapsing at training, so assistant Aaron Danks leads Bayern into Saturday's meeting with Borussia Dortmund - in the same week Harry Kane collected the Ballon d'Or.

title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Iraola backs Gravenberch as Arteta's touchline row rumbles on
standfirst: Andoni Iraola has defended Ryan Gravenberch ahead of Sunday's meeting with Arsenal, while Mikel Arteta arrives at Anfield still unhappy about how the technical-area rule is applied.

title: Juventus v Napoli: Spalletti under pressure, Allegri short at the back
standfirst: Two defeats in three matches have put Luciano Spalletti's position in question before Sunday's meeting with Napoli, who travel without Badiashile and Spinazzola but with Amir Rrahmani back.

title: Chelsea v Manchester United: Carrick insists the dressing room is not divided
standfirst: Eight games without a win, Benjamin Sesko out until January and public criticism from senior players: Manchester United travel to Stamford Bridge in turmoil.

title: Barcelona v Alavés: Flick considers Frenkie de Jong in defence amid injury crisis
standfirst: With defenders missing, Hansi Flick is ready to move Frenkie de Jong back into the defensive line - and has made it clear that Alejandro Balde is out of favour.

title: 616 days later: can De Zerbi's Spurs finally win three in a row?
standfirst: Tottenham have not won three Premier League games in succession since early 2025. A revived side under Roberto De Zerbi gets the chance against a Crystal Palace team in difficulty.

title: Milan derby with the title race tightening: Inter no longer on top
standfirst: Inter go into Saturday's Derby della Madonnina after Lazio overtook them at the top of Serie A, while the two Milan clubs have just revealed the name of their new stadium.

title: Leverkusen v Stuttgart: Werkself look for league reaction after Hoffenheim blow
standfirst: A 3-0 defeat at Hoffenheim and a cup scare against Nürnberg have shaken Leverkusen; Stuttgart arrive after a late cup winner from Deniz Undav.

title: PSV v Willem II: Streppel returns to a club with 'very little to hold on to'
standfirst: Bottom of the Eredivisie with two points from ten games and fresh from a 1-6 home defeat, Willem II travel to PSV under a familiar coach: Jurgen Streppel.

title: Udinese v Roma: unbeaten Roma carry their comeback spirit north
standfirst: Roma are still unbeaten in Serie A after twice coming from behind to draw 3-3 at Napoli. They visit Udinese on Saturday evening.

title: Ajax v AZ: Berghuis expected back as Ajax chase a fourth straight win
standfirst: Ajax have won three in a row and Míchel expects Steven Berghuis to return for the visit of AZ, with Daley Blind back after 1,433 days.

title: Man City v Brighton: leaders respond to first defeat as Hürzeler's side regroup
standfirst: Manchester City dropped their first league points of the season at Aston Villa. Brighton come to the Etihad after a 2-0 loss at Anfield that left Fabian Hürzeler taking a swipe at Liverpool.

title: Aston Villa v Fulham: Jackson and Suzuki carry Villa's feel-good factor
standfirst: Villa beat the league leaders last weekend; Fulham have won two in a row and climbed out of the relegation zone.

title: Lazio v Cagliari: Gattuso's leaders chase more history
standfirst: Twenty-two points from a possible 24 is the best start in Lazio's Serie A history. Gennaro Gattuso is still asking for calm.

title: Marseille v Toulouse: Genesio wants answers after the 4-3 scare against Le Havre
standfirst: Four goals up with half an hour left, Marseille almost threw it all away against bottom side Le Havre. Bruno Genesio has explained why he spared Angel Gomes from criticism.

title: Lyon v Angers: moved for the national day of protest, with injuries piling up
standfirst: The fixture was rescheduled at the request of the authorities. Lyon return to action after a 2-0 defeat at PSG and a growing injury list.

title: Frankfurt v Hamburg: a quick rematch after the cup, and an injury crisis for HSV
standfirst: Eintracht knocked Hamburg out of the DFB-Pokal on Tuesday. Merlin Polzin must now rebuild a depleted side for the league meeting.

title: Schalke v Leipzig: Hwang outburst overshadows Schalke's cup exit
standfirst: Schalke were knocked out of the cup by second-tier Dynamo Dresden. Leipzig, under pressure Martin Demichelis, arrive after a hard-fought cup win at Essen.

title: Feyenoord v Fortuna Sittard: leaders host Buijs as he chases a club record
standfirst: Feyenoord left Eindhoven as moral winners after a 1-1 draw. Fortuna coach Danny Buijs can become the most successful coach in the club's Eredivisie history.

title: Porto v Estoril: Farioli's side still perfect after nine league games
standfirst: Porto bounced back from their Champions League defeat to PSV and remain flawless in the league, with Benfica keeping pace.

title: Lecce v Genoa: De Rossi's Genoa ride a Bijlow wave
standfirst: Genoa beat Juventus 2-0 in midweek, with goalkeeper Justin Bijlow praised by Daniele De Rossi. Lecce are trying to recover from a 5-1 defeat.

title: Frosinone v Torino: the promoted side in sixth meet an Abate side in form
standfirst: Frosinone climbed to sixth after a 5-1 win over Lecce. Torino beat Monza 3-2 with goals from Fitz-Jim, Belghali and Vlasic.

title: Elche v Valencia: Aguirre's Valencia still searching for a spark
standfirst: One home win in nine, late defeats and a derby lost in stoppage time: Valencia travel to Elche under pressure.

title: Bournemouth v Leeds: Rose's Cherries on a high after Old Trafford
standfirst: Bournemouth won 3-0 at Manchester United, having already humbled AC Milan. Leeds arrive after a goalless draw at Sunderland.

title: Troyes v Le Mans: Le Mans arrive at the centre of the goal-line row
standfirst: A goal awarded by goal-line technology at Auxerre sparked one of the controversies of the season in France. Le Mans also lose Djibril Sidibé to a broken foot.
